items.summary_en: Ghizzano, a small village of a few hundred people in Tuscany, Italy, has been transformed into a colorful open-air art museum. Funds from a controversial local landfill allowed the mayor to invite contemporary artists, including British painter David Tremlett, to paint the village streets with vivid colors. The village, once forgotten, now attracts growing numbers of tourists and art lovers from across the region.
